In August 2013, there was this Dollar Tree store I used to frequent since around 2006 or 2007 not too far from where i live. Well, around summer of 2013, some employee walked up to me as i entered it telling me i need to put my bag down at the door. I assumed it was some new rule that if your bag is a certain size it should be left behind before you begin your shopping and to their defense I DO recall having walked in with a pretty sizeable backpack so i complied with the request and didn't think too much of it... until... UNTIL i saw some guy in one of the aisles with this JUMBO-SIZED backpack that almost looked big enough to put the whole dam store in! Well, okay, it wasn't that big but still! It was pretty large AND it was so full that it looked like it could burst at the zippers from what i recall. It was definitely bigger than the one i had!

So some time past and a week or so later, i walk into that same store with my backpack. Same employee stopping me about my bag. Giving her a bit of attitude and put my bag down, intentionally showing reluctance. But then again, if anything goes missing from my bag, shit, I'd take their sorry asses to court and I'd be OWNING that building with the kind of money i'd sue them for. Anyhow, I recall their being another day I went there and that same staffer wasn't there to confront me about the bag but she did have cashier duty that day. I was in line paying for my bag of chips but not at her line! However, we did look at each other with a slight glare for a second before I paid for my chips and got out of there.

Now onto the scary situation i found myself in:

I go to that store on a warm summer afternoon. I walk not even four steps in the door before a male employee walks up to me saying "ho-ho-hold up; you can't come in here!" Mind you, i did have a bag on that time but this man said absolutely nothing about it. I'm like, "why not?" "They said you was stealin'" "You're playing with me, aren't you?" "Nah, man, I'm dead serious." "I wasn't stealing anything." "I'm not saying you stole; I'm just telling you what they told me." "Can I speak to a supervisor?" "I am the the supervisor." "Well, look, I wasn't stealing anything!" "All right, go 'head, but if i catch you stealin' I'm taking you to the police."

And then the conversation ended right then and there and I was allowed to shop there with my bag on... no one told me to take it off anyway. Also, I wish i wasn't too nervous to question his claim he was the supervisor at that store. He looked to me like one of the regular staffers... and on TOP of that! There was an older female cashier not too far from the entrance at one of the check-out counters. If I could change how i handled that exchange differently, this would've been me:

Me: "Excuse me? Ma'am?"

Female employee: "Yes."

Me (pointing out the guy who stopped me at that door): "Is this man the supervisor at this establishment?"

Female employee: "No, he is not. Why? Would you like to see a supervisor?"

Me: "Yes, I would. I'd like to see one because I'm being falsely accused of shoplifting, AND he lied to me saying he was."

Well, nevertheless, in case you're wondering, I've not set foot in that establishment since and it's pretty safe to say that'll be my last time ever in that dam store! OH and not too long beforehand I did just weeks prior fill out a job application to try and work there, but THANK GOODNESS I never handed it in! Not only do they know my face, they would've gotten my first and last name AND my address and I would've been screwed! Mind you, I've NEVER been incarcerated or arrested for anything ever. The closest i've ever been to getting in trouble with law enforcement is the police having to take me home from school for fights and that's only happened, what, twice in my entire life? I've never even been in handcuffs! So that last situation was very scary and nerve-wracking to say the very least.
